standard_prerequisites.name: Equivalence of birationality with the existence of isomorphic nonempty opens
Existence of a rational map realising a prescribed isomorphism of local rings at generic points
A birational morphism induces an isomorphism on nonempty opens

core_obligations: From the third condition build the birational morphism and conclude (proof lines 13135-13144).
proof_roadmap: First equivalence and the immediate step (proof lines 13132-13134).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives three equivalent formulations of birationality for irreducible schemes locally of finite presentation over a base: being birational, admitting nonempty isomorphic opens, and having generic points over the same point of the base with isomorphic local rings as algebras over the local ring of that point. The proof quotes the equivalence of the first two, notes the immediate implication from the second to the third, and then, assuming the third, uses the rational-map existence result to build a birational morphism whose effect on nonempty opens is an isomorphism.
